title: Canonical ideal-power quotient towers of modules on algebraic spaces
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $X$ an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $N$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module on its small etale site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. On a chart $T\to X$ pull back $a\in A$ through $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ to $a_T\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. A map $f:N\to M$ kills $I^nN$ when $f_T(a_Ts)=0$ for every chart $T$, every $a\in I^n$ and every $s\in N(T)$. A quotient tower consists of module sheaves $Q_n$, maps $q_n:N\to Q_n$ killing $I^nN$, and, for every $r\geq n$, maps $t_{r,n}:Q_r\to Q_n$ with $q_rt_{r,n}=q_n$. Each $q_n$ has the full universal property: for every module $M$ and every map $f:N\to M$ killing $I^nN$, there is exactly one $d:Q_n\to M$ such that $q_nd=f$. Such a tower exists; between any two there is exactly one family of isomorphisms preserving the quotient projections. Define the canonical tower by this universal property. Equivalently $Q_n=N/(I\mathcal O_X)^nN$ is the sheaf cokernel, not the quotient of global sections, and $I^0=A$, so $Q_0=0$.
